title: H332 — QuantaAlpha: LLM Evolutionary Alpha Mining on H198 Universe
rationale: QuantaAlpha (arXiv:2602.07085) treats alpha mining as trajectory-level optimization: LLM proposes factor expressions, evaluates on historical data, then mutates/crosses successful ones like genetic programming. Enforces semantic consistency between hypothesis, factor code, and expression. Results: IC 0.1501, ARR 27.75%, MaxDD 7.98% on CSI 300; transfers to S&P 500 with 137% cumulative excess over 4 years. Applying this to the H198 30-stock universe could discover non-obvious factor combinations that pure momentum misses — specifically combinations of momentum, reversal, quality, and volatility signals that the evolutionary search would find but manual hypothesis generation would not.
content:
Script scaffold for H332 QuantaAlpha-inspired evolutionary alpha mining.

Approach: Simplified version without LLM in the loop (cost constraint).
1. Define a population of 20 candidate alpha expressions from known working signals (6-1m momentum, alpha101 subset, reversal, quality F-Score).
2. Evaluate each on IS 2013-2020: IC, Sharpe, MaxDD.
3. Select top-50% by Sharpe, recombine (weighted blend of 2 parent alphas), mutate (adjust lookback windows ±1m, swap scoring function).
4. Repeat for 5 generations.
5. Select best-evolved alpha, run OOS 2021-2026 ONCE.

Gate: OOS Sharpe > H198 1.174 AND IC > 0.05 AND no look-ahead bias.

Note: This is a simplified evolutionary search, not the full LLM-in-the-loop QuantaAlpha. The full version (with OpenAI API) is a future upgrade (H332b). H332 proves the evolutionary search mechanism works on this universe.

Key constraint: MUST use H198's same 30-stock universe and 6-1m base signal as seed. Evolution starts from known-good baseline, not random.
